endorsements.quote: It is up to us, as a multistakeholder community, to identify the right problems in oncology to solve, to develop the science and infrastructure necessary to build trust, to support clinicians and practices through digital transformation with the appropriate resources, and to reimagine the systems of research and care necessary for digital approaches to truly transform the life of every person living with cancer.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate digital solutions in oncology longitudinally, recognizing that their value may change with disease progression and evolving patient needs.
Develop and drive broad adoption of standardized methodological approaches for evaluating digital oncology solutions.
Deploy inclusive approaches to all digital solutions, using them to reach underserved populations and capture data on previously invisible populations.
Develop data governance frameworks that increase data liquidity through trustworthy, transparent data sharing and exchange.
Build evidence for payment innovation and novel incentive structures that favor adoption of digital health technologies in value-based care.
Define the context of use and the health concept of interest before deploying biometric monitoring technologies in research or clinical practice.
Select digital outcome measures that are meaningful to patients.
Prioritize digital solutions that support both patient privacy and information sharing.
Design digital solutions that are culturally competent and acceptable to every patient, and address the needs of care partners.
Use digital approaches to make culturally appropriate education materials accessible to patients and care partners.
Develop implementation parameters for deploying digital tools to support successful clinical implementation.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary summarizing findings and recommendations from a multistakeholder roundtable on advancing digital health and machine learning innovation in oncology.
